rows.title: Supplement Safety Knowledge, Information Sources, and Self-Reported Safety-Related Behaviors Among Adults Aged 40 Years and Older: A Pilot Study.
rows.focus: Cross-sectional pilot survey of 150 adults aged 40 years or older found high supplement use and frequent multi-supplement use. Associations between safety knowledge, information sources, and safety-related behaviors were limited and sensitive to outcome definition; findings are hypothesis-generating because of the modest convenience sample and self-reported measures.
rows.evidence_boundary: Observational pilot evidence; does not establish causal effects of information sources or safety knowledge on supplement-related outcomes.
